subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: For configured provider model entries, should audio/video and falsely declared image capability be rejected, accepted as metadata, or allowed only behind an explicit capability-source or override contract?
rationale: Current main preserves audio/video as public config metadata while docs and runtime selection still behave as if text/image are the only supported chat inputs, so an automated fix would encode product/API direction without maintainer approval.

options.title: Settle capability authority first
options.body: Choose the trusted source and override policy, then implement schema/runtime/docs/tests consistently around that decision.

options.title: Reject unsupported configured inputs
options.body: Tighten config validation for unsupported modalities and add a doctor migration or documented upgrade path for existing custom multimodal entries.

options.title: Accept metadata and guard routing
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid metadata but add runtime/catalog cross-checks and diagnostics so unsupported selected capabilities fail clearly before deployment or routing.

recommendation.title: Settle capability authority first
recommendation.body: Choose the trusted source and override policy, then implement schema/runtime/docs/tests consistently around that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provider/model catalog architecture, runtime routing, docs, and compatibility policy where recent history shows broad adjacent ownership.
